the weakening of indigenous languages and practices by globalisation and urban migration
the ceremony that marks a person's movement from one social status to another
a practice forbidden by custom because it is considered sacred or harmful
items.s: Endangerment of culture: the weakening of indigenous languages and practices by globalisation and urban migration. The other options describe Rite of passage, Taboo, Culture lag.

items.q: Nationally recognised works may be defined as
o: the Nigerian national anthem and pledge that express unity, honour and service to the fatherland
the hourglass drum used among the Yoruba, called the gangan, which imitates speech tones
the woven cloth of the Ukwuani people of Abia State produced on a vertical loom
the ancient Nigerian society of the Jos plateau known for its terracotta figurines
items.s: Nationally recognised works: the Nigerian national anthem and pledge that express unity, honour and service to the fatherland. The other options describe Akwete cloth, Talking drum, Nok culture.

items.q: “the view that a culture should be judged by its own standards rather than by another's” is the definition of
o: Material culture
Endangerment of culture
Ethnocentrism
Cultural relativism
items.s: Cultural relativism is the view that a culture should be judged by its own standards rather than by another's.

items.q: “the Yoruba festival held in honour of the goddess of the Osun river” is the definition of
o: Argungu fishing festival
Ancestor veneration
Osun Osogbo
Chi
items.s: Osun Osogbo is the Yoruba festival held in honour of the goddess of the Osun river.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Talking drum among Igbo.
o: the slit drum called the oja or ikoro used to send messages over distance
the naturalistic metal and terracotta heads produced by the Yoruba city of Ile-Ife
the archaeological site near Awka where ninth century bronze objects were found
the hand woven cloth of the Yoruba used for important ceremonies
items.s: Talking drum among Igbo: the slit drum called the oja or ikoro used to send messages over distance. The other options describe Ife bronze heads, Aso oke, Igbo-Ukwu.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Acculturation?
o: the weakening of indigenous languages and practices by globalisation and urban migration
the process of building loyalty to the nation across ethnic, religious and regional divides
the ideas, beliefs, norms and values of a people
the change that occurs when two cultures come into sustained contact
items.s: Acculturation: the change that occurs when two cultures come into sustained contact. The other options describe National integration, Endangerment of culture, Non material culture.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Rite of passage?
o: the habit of judging other cultures as inferior to one's own
a practice forbidden by custom because it is considered sacred or harmful
the ceremony that marks a person's movement from one social status to another
the change that occurs when two cultures come into sustained contact
items.s: Rite of passage: the ceremony that marks a person's movement from one social status to another. The other options describe Taboo, Ethnocentrism, Acculturation.

items.q: The correct meaning of Afro-Asiatic family is
o: the language family that includes Hausa, Arabic and the Chadic languages
the largest language family in Africa, covering the Yoruba, Igbo, Tiv, Ibibio and Efik languages
the ability of a person or community to use more than one language
the widely spoken contact language that draws its vocabulary mainly from English
items.s: Afro-Asiatic family: the language family that includes Hausa, Arabic and the Chadic languages. The other options describe Niger-Congo family, Multilingualism, Nigerian Pidgin.

items.q: In this course, Igbo-Ukwu refers to
o: the Nigerian national anthem and pledge that express unity, honour and service to the fatherland
the ancient Nigerian society of the Jos plateau known for its terracotta figurines
the indigo resist-dyed cloth of the Yoruba people of Abeokuta
the archaeological site near Awka where ninth century bronze objects were found
items.s: Igbo-Ukwu: the archaeological site near Awka where ninth century bronze objects were found. The other options describe Adire, Nok culture, Nationally recognised works.

items.q: The correct meaning of Widowhood rites is
o: the system in which descent and inheritance are traced through the father's line
the system in which descent is traced through the mother's line
the network of relationships based on descent and marriage
the customary observances imposed on a woman after the death of her husband
items.s: Widowhood rites: the customary observances imposed on a woman after the death of her husband. The other options describe Patrilineal descent, Kinship, Matrilineal descent.

items.q: In this course, Oba refers to
o: the title of the divine king among the Yoruba and the Edo
the Yoruba empire whose Alaafin ruled with the Oyo Mesi council and the Bashorun
an association such as the Ozo or Ekpe through which prestige and authority are earned
the acephalous Igbo system in which the village assembly and the council of elders governed
items.s: Oba: the title of the divine king among the Yoruba and the Edo. The other options describe Igbo village republic, Title society, Oyo empire.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Age grade.
o: the empire of the Lake Chad region ruled by the Mai and later the Shehu of Bornu
the centralised system of the Hausa-Fulani north in which an emir ruled through district heads on Islamic principles
the system in which people born within a similar period form a group that shares duties and ceremonies
the kingdom of the Benue valley ruled by the Aku Uka of Wukari
items.s: Age grade: the system in which people born within a similar period form a group that shares duties and ceremonies. The other options describe Jukun kingdom, Kanem-Bornu, Emirate system.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Osun Osogbo.
o: the Kebbi festival held at the end of the fishing season on the Matan Fada river
a deity in the Yoruba traditional religious system
the indigenous belief system that honours a supreme being through deities, ancestors and spirits
the Yoruba festival held in honour of the goddess of the Osun river
items.s: Osun Osogbo: the Yoruba festival held in honour of the goddess of the Osun river. The other options describe Argungu fishing festival, Traditional religion, Orisha.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Taboo.
o: the peaceful coexistence of groups with different traditions, which national life requires
a practice forbidden by custom because it is considered sacred or harmful
the ceremony that marks a person's movement from one social status to another
the view that a culture should be judged by its own standards rather than by another's
items.s: Taboo: a practice forbidden by custom because it is considered sacred or harmful. The other options describe Cultural relativism, Harmony, Rite of passage.

items.q: The correct meaning of Emirate system is
o: the system in which people born within a similar period form a group that shares duties and ceremonies
the acephalous Igbo system in which the village assembly and the council of elders governed
the centralised system of the Hausa-Fulani north in which an emir ruled through district heads on Islamic principles
the kingdom of the Benue valley ruled by the Aku Uka of Wukari
items.s: Emirate system: the centralised system of the Hausa-Fulani north in which an emir ruled through district heads on Islamic principles. The other options describe Age grade, Jukun kingdom, Igbo village republic.

items.q: The correct meaning of Ethnicity is
o: the federal capital territory chosen in 1976 and made the capital in 1991
the joining of the Northern and Southern Protectorates into one colony by Lord Lugard
the identification of people by common descent, language and culture, a factor in Nigerian politics
the local administrative body built around a traditional ruler under indirect rule
items.s: Ethnicity: the identification of people by common descent, language and culture, a factor in Nigerian politics. The other options describe Native authority, Abuja, Amalgamation of 1914.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Osun Osogbo?
o: the personal spirit or destiny in Igbo belief
the practice of honouring deceased forebears believed to watch over the living
the peaceful coexistence of adherents of different faiths, a recurring theme in Nigerian national life
the Yoruba festival held in honour of the goddess of the Osun river
items.s: Osun Osogbo: the Yoruba festival held in honour of the goddess of the Osun river. The other options describe Chi, Interreligious tolerance, Ancestor veneration.

items.q: In this course, Non material culture refers to
o: the ideas, beliefs, norms and values of a people
the ceremony that marks a person's movement from one social status to another
the physical objects a people make and use, such as tools, dress and buildings
a practice forbidden by custom because it is considered sacred or harmful
items.s: Non material culture: the ideas, beliefs, norms and values of a people. The other options describe Taboo, Rite of passage, Material culture.

items.q: In this course, Harmony refers to
o: the peaceful coexistence of groups with different traditions, which national life requires
exchange of ideas, artistic richness and broader national identity
the ideas, beliefs, norms and values of a people
the weakening of indigenous languages and practices by globalisation and urban migration
items.s: Harmony: the peaceful coexistence of groups with different traditions, which national life requires. The other options describe Non material culture, Endangerment of culture, Benefits of cultural diversity.

items.q: In this course, Matrilineal descent refers to
o: the system in which descent and inheritance are traced through the father's line
the system in which descent is traced through the mother's line
the traditional practice of arranging a marriage partner for a child before maturity
the household made up of a husband, wife or wives and their children
items.s: Matrilineal descent: the system in which descent is traced through the mother's line. The other options describe Child betrothal, Patrilineal descent, Nuclear family.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Edo?
o: the ethnic group of the Niger Delta whose livelihood rests largely on fishing and the creeks
the ethnic group of Cross River State known for the Ekpe secret society and the town of Calabar
the ethnic group of Benin City, historically the people of the great Benin kingdom
the ethnic group of the Lake Chad basin, historically the ruling people of the Kanem-Bornu empire
items.s: Edo: the ethnic group of Benin City, historically the people of the great Benin kingdom. The other options describe Kanuri, Ijaw, Efik.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Ethnocentrism?
o: the physical objects a people make and use, such as tools, dress and buildings
the process of building loyalty to the nation across ethnic, religious and regional divides
the habit of judging other cultures as inferior to one's own
the peaceful coexistence of groups with different traditions, which national life requires
items.s: Ethnocentrism: the habit of judging other cultures as inferior to one's own. The other options describe Harmony, Material culture, National integration.
